# Best travel chargers with multiple USB-C ports

**Best overall: UGREEN Nexode 100W 4-Port GaN charger.** It has 3 USB-C ports and 1 USB-A. Either of the first two USB-C ports can deliver the full 100W alone. With a laptop and a second device it splits 65W/30W, and with all four ports in use it splits 45W/30W/10.5W. It's the heaviest of the three TechWise picks at 8.3 oz. TechWise and VoyageHacks both rank it at or near the top. TechWise says its reviews are based on specs and user feedback, not hands-on testing. ([TechWise](https://www.techwisereviews.com/posts/best-gan-usb-c-chargers-travel-2026), [VoyageHacks](https://voyagehacks.com/en/travel-gear/best-gan-wall-chargers-for-travel/))

**Other picks:**
- **Anker Prime 67W 3-Port (lightest):** It has 2 USB-C ports and 1 USB-A, weighs about 4.78 oz, and has foldable prongs. It also supports PPS, so Samsung and Pixel phones charge at full speed. It delivers 67W to one device and drops to about 65W across two. It's enough for a MacBook Air or most 13-14" ultrabooks. ([VoyageHacks](https://voyagehacks.com/en/travel-gear/best-gan-wall-chargers-for-travel/))
- **Anker 737 GaNPrime 120W (power-hungry laptops):** It has 2 USB-C ports and 1 USB-A. It's the pick if one demanding laptop is your priority. ([TechWise](https://www.techwisereviews.com/posts/best-usb-c-chargers-travel-multiple-devices-2026))
- **Baseus GaN5 Pro 65W (the one I can link to buy):** It has 2 USB-C ports and 1 USB-A, with PPS and foldable prongs. It's **$49.99 for a 2-pack** (list $59.99), so you get one for home and one for the bag. With multiple devices connected, the laptop port drops to 45W, which is fine for a MacBook Air but not a 65W laptop. Warranty is 18–24 months. [Buy at Baseus's US store](https://dealectric.com/go/baseus-gan5-pro-65w-2c-u). This is an affiliate link, and the page says the price was verified 2026-10-21.

**If you want a charger with built-in international plugs:** Android Central recommends the Baseus EnerCore CG11 (70W, retractable USB-C cable), the Epicka TA-105 Max (75W, 3 USB-C ports) and the UGREEN 65W Nexode 3-port travel adapter. ([Android Central](https://www.androidcentral.com/accessories/power-charging/best-usb-adapter-for-travel))

**Things to know before buying:**
- Ports share power. Put your laptop on the port that keeps its full wattage, and use the other ports for phones and earbuds.
- Outside North America you need a plug-shape adapter, not a voltage converter. Most of these chargers accept 100-240V.
- For a true 100W, you need an e-marked 5A USB-C cable.
- For just a phone, tablet and earbuds, a 65W charger is plenty. Go to 100W only if your laptop needs it. ([DeviceJoy](https://devicejoy.com/guides/best-usb-c-chargers-for-international-travel/))

I didn't get direct purchase links for the UGREEN or Anker models. The "Check price" buttons on the TechWise and VoyageHacks pages link to current listings. If you tell me your laptop and phone, I can say which wattage you actually need.
